headline_marked: NCP leader alleges [[MP-led 'mob rule' in Mirpur]] as health center looted
headline: NCP leader alleges MP-led 'mob rule' in Mirpur as health center looted
summary: Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain accuses MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty of leading the destruction of a 50-year-old health center and lootings at Salman Muqtadir's studio.
details: National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has accused reserved women’s seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty of leading the looting and demolition of the Radda MCH office and health centre in Mirpur.
The facility, which provided free primary healthcare, maternity services, and family planning to poor mothers and children for five decades, was attacked late Thursday night using heavy machinery.

Asif Mahmud noted that vaccines for poor children, along with medicines and equipment, were looted from the clinic. He also linked the attacks to the recent vandalism of content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.
The NCP leader criticized the police for arriving only after the incidents had occurred, comparing the response to a trope from Bangla films.

Asif called for a neutral investigation committee to investigate the vandalism at both the health center and the studio, alleging organized crime involving the BNP MP, city corporation administrator, and local police.
He warned that if swift justice is not served, it would imply that the highest levels of government, including the prime minister, are aware of the incidents and share the blame.
The NCP has demanded that the damages be evaluated, compensation paid, and the health center be rebuilt to resume essential services.
caption:
Vaccines for poor children looted? NCP leader slams 'mob rule' and an MP's alleged role in Mirpur's destruction.

National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has accused reserved women’s seat MP Ferdousi Ahmed Misty of leading the looting and demolition of the Radda MCH office and health centre in Mirpur.

The facility, which provided free primary healthcare, maternity services, and family planning to poor mothers and children for five decades, was attacked late Thursday night using heavy machinery.

Asif Mahmud noted that vaccines for poor children, along with medicines and equipment, were looted from the clinic. He also linked the attacks to the recent vandalism of content creator Salman Muqtadir's studio.

The NCP leader criticized the police for arriving only after the incidents had occurred, comparing the response to a trope from Bangla films.

Asif called for a neutral investigation committee to investigate the vandalism at both the health center and the studio, alleging organized crime involving the BNP MP, city corporation administrator, and local police.

He warned that if swift justice is not served, it would imply that the highest levels of government, including the prime minister, are aware of the incidents and share the blame.

The NCP has demanded that the damages be evaluated, compensation paid, and the health center be rebuilt to resume essential services.

headline: PM Tarique Rahman returns home after five-day US visit
summary: The Prime Minister has returned to Bangladesh after attending the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has arrived back in Bangladesh following a five-day official visit to the United States.
The Prime Minister's visit to New York was primarily to attend the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) session.
During his stay in the US, the Prime Minister engaged in various high-level meetings and represented Bangladesh on the global stage.
En route to Dhaka, the Prime Minister made a brief stop in Dubai.
Upon his arrival in the country, he was received by high-ranking officials and party leaders.
caption:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is back in Bangladesh after a five-day diplomatic mission to the US.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has arrived back in Bangladesh following a five-day official visit to the United States.

The Prime Minister's visit to New York was primarily to attend the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) session.

During his stay in the US, the Prime Minister engaged in various high-level meetings and represented Bangladesh on the global stage.

En route to Dhaka, the Prime Minister made a brief stop in Dubai.

Upon his arrival in the country, he was received by high-ranking officials and party leaders.
